summary: This article explains how slightly acidic rainwater carves limestone caves, how dripping water builds stalactites, stalagmites, and columns, and what Saudi Arabia's caves reveal about the past.
introduce: Show the title “Caves and Their Stone Icicles” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a kind of rock that water can slowly wear away
to break down and mix completely into a liquid
a natural solid material found in rocks and the ground

challengeTerms.def: a substance that can slowly eat away or break down other materials
a common mineral that makes up limestone and cave formations
to leave a layer of material behind

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that cave formations should be protected, even if it means fewer people can visit caves? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how water both destroys rock and builds new stone inside a cave.
struggling: Pre-teach limestone, dissolve, and mineral with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use acid, calcite, and deposit in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
